title: More momentum, faster descent?
hook: Letting the ball keep its speed gets it downhill faster. Can you have too much?

knows: that gradient descent steps downhill on a loss surface
doesNotKnow: that remembering previous steps (momentum) speeds descent along a valley
that too much momentum overshoots and slows it down again

objective: The learner can explain that momentum smooths the zigzag and speeds progress along a long valley, but that too much carries the ball past the bottom repeatedly, so there is a sweet spot.

claims.text: The toy valley is f = ½(x² + 25y²), started at (4, 1) with step size 0.07; each step sets velocity = momentum × previous velocity − 0.07 × slope, then moves by the velocity, until within 0.1 of the bottom.
claims.source: The lesson's own model in Demo.tsx (descend). The valley is invented; real loss surfaces are not this shape.

claims.text: Steps to get within 0.1 of the bottom: 51 with no momentum, 21 at 0.5, 19 at 0.8, 30 at 0.9.
claims.source: Deterministic iteration (no randomness): stepsFor() in Demo.tsx, and the category manager's script; reproduced by the builder in node with the same rule.

claims.text: At momentum 0.9 the ball overshoots the bottom along the valley three times (furthest to x = -2.17) before settling.
claims.source: Sign changes of x along descend(0.9) in Demo.tsx (builder's node script): 3 crossings, minimum x -2.17. At 0.8 there is 1 crossing (to -1.03); at 0 and 0.5 none.

claims.text: This velocity rule is heavy-ball momentum, widely used to train neural networks.
claims.source: Polyak 1964, 'Some methods of speeding up the convergence of iteration methods', USSR Computational Mathematics and Mathematical Physics 4(5); Goodfellow, Bengio & Courville 2016, Deep Learning, §8.3.2.

recall.question: Training is slow, so someone raises momentum from 0.8 to 0.99. Training gets slower and the loss swings up and down. Why?
options: Too much momentum keeps carrying the model past the minimum
Momentum has no effect, so it must be the data
Higher momentum always means smaller steps
recall.why: Momentum keeps part of the previous step's velocity. A little smooths zigzags and speeds descent; too much carries the parameters past the bottom again and again, so progress slows and the loss oscillates.
